sections.text: US negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff reportedly asked if Ukraine would cede the Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership or security guarantees. Volodymyr Zelenskyy also accused SpaceX of re-imposing speed limits on its Starshield satellite system, restricting Ukrainian drones to 161km/h. SpaceX denied making any changes to the service.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The Starshield restrictions reportedly hamper Ukraine's ability to intercept jet-powered Russian drones. sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: SpaceX launched its 15th Starship test flight from South Texas. A planned catch of the lower booster stage failed on Friday when it diverted and exploded in the Gulf of Mexico. On Saturday, SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage using mechanical arms on its launch tower for the first time.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The upper-stage catch is a key milestone in making Starship rapidly reusable. Nasa has contracted SpaceX to return humans to the lunar surface using the vehicle, and SpaceX also plans future missions to Mars.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: SpaceX is investigating what caused the booster landing abort. Chief executive Elon Musk plans to increase Starship test flights to a weekly, then twice-weekly frequency.

sections.text: West Sussex experienced record heatwaves and severe drought, causing stress to traditional plants and killing some trees and rhododendrons. Globally, 2026 saw extreme weather including deadly heatwaves, floods, mudslides, typhoons and wildfires across multiple continents.

sections.text: Traditional plant species are failing to survive in changing conditions, threatening garden displays. On a global scale, extreme weather has killed tens of thousands of people, displaced communities, damaged infrastructure and pushed Earth's climate indicators to extreme levels.

sections.heading: What happened

sections.text: Historically, Indigenous contributions to the 1804 expedition were downplayed, and Native Americans often view that history as an invasion. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Tesla offered select customers the chance to purchase a Cybercab for personal use in supported service areas. The car costs $29,990 with a $1,000 non-refundable deposit and a mandatory $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription. Initial availability is limited, and buyers cannot use the vehicle for commercial purposes or add it to Tesla's Robotaxi network.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The mandatory subscription brings the real baseline cost over five years to roughly $47,600. Cancelling the subscription renders the car completely unusable on public roads as there is no manual fallback. Furthermore, early buyers face regulatory uncertainty while the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration audits the self-certification of a vehicle without steering wheels or pedals.

gist: A federal judge temporarily blocked Donald Trump from closing a historic Washington golf course.
Judge Ana Reyes ruled the administration broke federal laws to meet an arbitrary deadline.
The decision keeps East Potomac Park open to the public until 28 November.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US District Judge Ana Reyes temporarily stopped the US government from shutting down East Potomac Park and its golf course in Washington DC. President Donald Trump intended to close the 106-year-old site to begin a 15-month redevelopment project. However, Reyes stated that the administration violated federal laws and offered pretextual reasons for the closure.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Campaigners and local residents sued to protect the historic public space, arguing the redevelopment would alter its character and raise costs. The ruling marks another judicial challenge to Trump's plans to alter the capital's architecture. Reyes has also launched an inquiry into whether government attorneys misled the court.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The temporary restraining order remains in effect until 28 November. Although the park must stay open, the government is not required to actively maintain golf operations. Meanwhile, a special master will assist an inquiry into the conduct of Justice Department lawyers.

Criminals exploit the trust people place in everyday security verifications.
Users can protect themselves by pausing, checking security software, and contacting their bank if compromised.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Criminals are using a tactic known as the ClickFix scam, which tricks users visiting websites into believing they need to prove they are human by pressing specific keys like the Windows Key, R, Ctrl, V, and Enter. This action copies and pastes malicious code to infect the computer with malware.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: According to researchers, this has become one of the most popular and sophisticated ways to deliver malware because people are accustomed to solving Captchas daily and trust standard security prompts.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: If a computer is compromised, users are advised to contact their bank immediately and change their passwords, prioritising the most important ones first.

sections.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps launched six drones targeting a US military radar in Bahrain on Sunday. Bahrain stated its air defences intercepted the drones. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden confirmed that a staggered age of consent will be discussed. The proposal follows the conviction of comedian Russell Brand, who was jailed for 10-and-a-half years for rape and sexual assault. Campaigner Mia Latter, who alleged abuse by Brand when she was 16, wants relationships between adults and 16 to 17-year-olds criminalised while permitting teenage relationships.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Under UK law, adults of any age can legally have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds. Campaign group Close the Consent Gap argues this creates a power imbalance, as people of this age are classified as children in other legal frameworks. Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary Helen Whately supported having a debate on changing the law.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Pat McFadden said he could not predict the conclusion of age of consent discussions. Meanwhile, Metropolitan Police are investigating comedian David Walliams over alleged serious sexual offences following reports by ITV News and the Guardian, which Walliams strongly denies.

gist: Zelenskyy blamed Starshield speed restrictions for enabling Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure.
Estonia will close border crossings with Russia following a suspected Russian sabotage attack.
Allies prepare meetings of the Coalition of the Willing and the Ramstein group.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that restrictions on Starshield terminals enabled Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Attacks affected eight regions, damaging power networks. Meanwhile, Estonia announced it will close all border crossings with Russia after a suspected sabotage attack on a drone manufacturer.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Starshield restrictions have reportedly hindered Ukrainian drone interceptions and mid-range strikes. Estonia linked the sabotage to its ongoing support for Ukraine, while Russian officials labelled border closures as Russophobia.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Estonia will close its border crossings on 1 December. Allied nations will meet at the Ramstein group next week to confirm continued support for Ukraine.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will argue at the Lord Mayor's Banquet that a needlessly hard Brexit created business barriers and failed to deliver on promises. Ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit, Burnham plans to sign deals on food, energy and youth mobility negotiated by predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Burnham set out three tests for agreements, including consistency with Labour's manifesto pledge of no return to the single market, customs union, or freedom of movement. Opponents criticised the move: Conservatives warned against drag into the EU, while Reform UK, Liberal Democrats and Green Party of England and Wales offered contrasting views.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Burnham wants to examine long-term options ranging from no changes to rejoining the single market. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Burnham will detail options after the summit. However, Burnham ruled out major changes before the next general election, stating a public mandate is required.

The pilot scheme aims to host around 100 asylum seekers with rejected claims.
Human Rights Watch criticised the proposal, citing Rwanda's record of human rights abuses.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Five EU nations – Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands – plan to establish a deportation hub in Kigali, Rwanda. The facility will target asylum seekers who have exhausted all legal options to stay within the EU. It follows EU reforms permitting return hubs outside the bloc.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The move reflects a broader EU effort to increase deportations and control irregular migration. However, Human Rights Watch warned that paying Rwanda could cause harm, financing a government linked to domestic repression, detention ill-treatment and armed rebels in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The proposed pilot scheme aims to host around 100 people, with each nation sending about 20 migrants. Participating countries hope the centre will be operational in 2027, while the UN's International Organisation for Migration may provide support.

sections.heading: What happened

timeline.text: Bompastor's risks pay off as Chelsea go top of WSL

gist: Sonia Bompastor made bold early substitutions as Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0.
Veerle Buurman replaced Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes in and successfully marshalled Khadija Shaw.
The victory sent Chelsea back to the top of the Women's Super League table.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Chelsea defeated Manchester City 1-0 in a Women's Super League match. Chelsea manager Sonia Bompastor substituted defender Kadeisha Buchanan twelve minutes into the game. Buchanan's replacement Veerle Buurman performed well, helping to quieten City striker Khadija Shaw. Sandy Baltimore scored the opening goal for Chelsea before being substituted at half-time. In the second half, City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita received a straight red card for bringing down Alyssa Thompson, ending the visitors' comeback hopes.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The narrow victory moved Chelsea back to the summit of the Women's Super League table, one point above Manchester City. Bompastor's risky tactical decisions proved to be the decisive factor in a tight top-of-the-table clash.

gist: Wales beat New Zealand 35-28 to secure their first victory against them in 73 years.
The match took place in Cardiff at the Principality Stadium in front of 55,152 fans.
A resilient defensive display in the final quarter helped Wales hold off the All Blacks.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Wales defeated New Zealand 35-28 in a nine-try Nations Championship match at the Principality Stadium, ending a 34-match losing sequence stretching back to 1953. Tries from Tomos Williams, Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit helped Wales build a lead. New Zealand responded through Cortez Ratima, Wallace Sititi, Fehi Fineanganofo and Peter Lakai, but Wales held firm with a crucial defensive display.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The win broke a 73-year winless run against the All Blacks, lifting a nation and providing a famous moment for Welsh rugby after a difficult period on and off the field.

At the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.
A brilliant performance and resilient defence gave Wales their first win against New Zealand since 1953.
